meaning: The number 61 has no prominent or well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
description: Unlike numbers such as 7, 12, 40 or 70, which carry deep symbolic resonance in the Bible and Jewish tradition, the number 61 has no special theological meaning in Scripture. It does not appear as a symbolically charged number in biblical texts. In Numbers 31:39, the number 61 is mentioned as the tribute to the Lord from donkeys after the war against the Midianites, but this is purely a numerical statement without symbolic weight. Within Kabbalistic gematria, however, the number does hold some mystical resonance through its connection to the Hebrew word אַיִן (ayin, "nothing"), though this is not an widely recognized biblical symbol value.

footnotes.text: In gematria, the Hebrew word אַיִן (ayin, "nothing" or "no thing") has the value 61 (alef = 1, yod = 10, nun = 50). Within Kabbalistic thought, the concept of ayin is linked to the divine origin prior to creation—the transcendent "nothing" from which all things emerge. This gives the number 61 a certain mystical resonance in Kabbalah, even though it is not an widely recognized symbolic value.

The levy of 61 donkeys in Numbers 31:39 results from a fixed rate of one out of every 500 taken from the soldiers' half of the war spoils (a total of 30,500 donkeys). Thus, the number has no independent symbolic function in the text but is simply the product of the prescribed distribution formula.
